newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower, seen consolidating.

text.p: Late selling pulled Taiwan share prices to finish lower on Tuesday and brokers said they expected a quiet consolidation in the near term.
The weighted index reversed its modest early gains to close 35.85 points or 0.52 percent lower at 6,855.57.
Turnover was a very subdued T$42.4 billion.
Brokers said a lack of new market-moving factors and recent slugglishness in overseas market had cooled buying interest.
"The market lacks momentum to challenge new highs so selling pressure naturally emerges," said Lin Long-hsien, an assistant manager of United Securities.

First International Computer, Taiwan's number two computer maker, outperformed the weak market, rising T$1 or 1.94 percent to T$52.5 after raising its 1996 pretax profit target to T$1.58 billion from a previous forecast of T$1.21 billion.
The entire electronic and machinery sector fell 0.35 percent despite First International's rise.
Plastics were hit hardest, falling 1.08 percent. Textile giant Hualon Corp lost 40 cents or 1.57 percent to T$25.
"Overall sentiment is quite conservative and it's likely to stay that way until the end of the year," Lin said.
Stocks that had lagged previous gains drew minor bargain hunting, with construction shares rebounding 0.05 percent.
Yuh Chen Construction topped the gainers' list, up T$2.3 or 6.76 percent to T$36.3.
Brokers said the market was likely to consolidate between 6,800 and 7,000 points in the near term.
